title: How Do Noise Cancelling Headphones Work?
caption: Noise cancelling fights sound with more sound: a mirror-image wave that cancels steady noise like engines and hums.
pinned_comment: Noise cancelling or transparency mode, which do you use? 👇

lines.text: Your headphones delete noise by making more noise.
A tiny microphone on the outside listens to the world around you.
A chip creates the exact mirror image of that sound, a wave flipped upside down.
Where a peak of the noise meets a dip of the anti-noise, they cancel out.
A second microphone inside the ear cup checks what still gets through and keeps correcting.
It works best on steady, low sounds, like plane engines, train rumble, or an air conditioner's hum.
Low sounds are long, slow waves, so the anti-noise has time to line up.
Sudden, high sounds change too fast. By the time the chip reacts, the wave has moved on.
That's why the engine hum fades, but the baby two rows back still gets through.
And that's why the ear cushions still matter. They block much of what the electronics miss.
So the next time a plane suddenly goes quiet, remember…
